hero.eyebrow: Coaching and headhunting - Amsterdam and Europe
hero.headline1: You're good at what you do.
hero.sub: Sometimes it's positioning. Sometimes it's access. Sometimes it's confidence. The work is finding which one, and fixing it. Coaching for senior professionals moving to or building careers across Europe, and search for the companies trying to hire them. By Alon Gildoni, Amsterdam.

track.heading: What actually happens.
track.sub: I work with a small number of professionals who have meaningful experience, and I do not take everyone on. Here is how it has gone so far.
track.splitNote: About half of the people I work with come from non-tech roles: HR, project management, finance, legal, and more.
track.selectNote: I work with a small number of people who have real experience, so each one gets genuine attention.
track.disclaimer: The numbers are strong, but there is no promise or guarantee of a job. Demand, industry, and luck all play a part.

pillars.heading: What makes the difference.
pillars.d1: Most career help comes from one side only: a coach who has never hired, or a recruiter who has never coached. I have spent years doing both. That is the difference between advice that sounds right and advice that actually works.
pillars.a1: Coach and headhunter, in one person.
pillars.t2: A real network, not a database
pillars.d2: Since 2018, TechExpats has grown into one of Europe's most connected communities of professionals. Introductions happen because the relationships are real, not because a tool scraped a profile.
pillars.d3: Building a career or a team across borders is its own skill: the unwritten rules of Dutch directness, the gap between one country's CV and another's, the things nobody tells you. That fluency is built in.

serve.heading: Two sides of the same table.
serve.coHeading: Your next move, made with a clear head.
serve.coBody: Whether you are job hunting, feeling stuck, relocating to Europe, or aiming for a bigger role, you do not need more generic advice. You need someone who knows how hiring really works and will be honest with you. That is the work we do together.
serve.coItem1: Job-search strategy, CV, and a LinkedIn that gets noticed
serve.coItem2: Interview preparation, including the Dutch and European context
serve.coItem3: Executive and leadership coaching for senior professionals
serve.coItem4: Relocation and career navigation across Europe
serve.taHeading: The hire you cannot afford to get wrong.
serve.taBody: Some roles are too important, too senior, or too specialised for a job board. I find the people who are not looking, assess them properly, and present a short list you can actually decide from. A small number of searches at a time, each given real attention.
serve.taItem2: Access to strong candidates who ignore job boards

spec.heading: Services.
spec.sub: A focused set of services for individuals building careers and companies building teams, all centred on one thing: the right match.
spec.d1: One-to-one coaching for professionals who want a sharper strategy, a stronger position in the market, and a plan that actually moves.
spec.d2: Preparation that goes past rehearsed answers: how to tell your story, handle the hard questions, and read a Dutch or European interview room.
spec.d3: For senior leaders facing a new role, a new country, or a difficult decision. A discreet sounding board, not a script.
spec.d4: Senior and specialist recruitment for companies. I reach the people who are not applying and present a short, properly vetted list.
spec.d5: Help for companies hiring into Europe: where the talent is, what it costs, how to position the role, and how to win the candidate.
spec.d6: For professionals moving to the Netherlands or across Europe: the market, the cultural code, and the practical path to the right role.

approach.heading: A process built around you.
approach.body: No volume, no spray and pray. Every engagement, whether I am coaching a person or running a search for a company, starts the same way: by understanding what success actually looks like, then working back from there.
approach.s1body: We start with the honest conversation. For a professional: what do you actually want, and what is holding it back? For a company: what is the real problem behind the hire? This is where the work is won.
approach.s2body: Then we use the network and the method. For individuals, that means positioning, introductions, and preparation that lands. For companies, it means reaching the people who are not on the market and approaching them properly.
approach.s3body: A great outcome is not a fast one, it is one that still looks right twelve months later. I stay close through the offer, the start, and the first hard decisions, on both sides.

beyond.heading: The relationship does not end at the offer.
beyond.body: The strongest work continues after the decision. Once someone is in the role, the first months decide everything. I often stay involved as a quiet sounding board, for the new leader and for the company that hired them.
beyond.i1body: The first three months in a new role or a new country make or break it. A trusted second opinion when it matters most.
beyond.i2body: A confidential thinking partner for senior professionals facing a hard call, a new team, or an unfamiliar culture.
beyond.i3body: Translating between Israeli, Dutch, and wider European working cultures. The subtext is where careers and deals are won or lost.
beyond.tagline: An extension of the work. Never a separate pitch.

about.quote: “Most people do not have a talent problem. They have a positioning problem, an access problem, or a confidence problem. My job is to find which one, and fix it.”
about.bio1: I have spent my career on both sides of hiring: as the person companies call to find talent they cannot find themselves, and as the coach professionals call when a career is stuck or about to change.
about.bio2: That combination is rare, and it is the whole point. A coach who has never hired is guessing. A recruiter who has never coached is matching keywords. I do both, every week, so the advice you get is grounded in how the market actually behaves.

aboutPage.name: Alon Gildoni
aboutPage.tagline: I help people build careers that fit, and help companies hire the people who change their trajectory.
aboutPage.introHeading: On both sides of every hire.
aboutPage.intro1: I am Alon Gildoni. For more than a decade I have worked at the meeting point of people and companies: finding talent that others cannot find, and coaching professionals through the moves that define a career.
aboutPage.intro2: Most people in this field do one or the other. I do both, deliberately, because each makes the other sharper. Coaching keeps me honest about how candidates really think. Search keeps me honest about how companies really decide.
aboutPage.bothHeading: Why that combination matters to you
aboutPage.both1: When I coach you, you are not getting motivational advice. You are getting the view from the other side of the table: what actually gets a CV read, why good people get passed over, what a hiring manager is really worried about, and how to position yourself so the answer is yes.
aboutPage.both2: When I run a search for your company, you are not getting a keyword match. You are getting someone who has sat with hundreds of professionals, understands what moves them, and can have the honest conversation that turns a strong passive candidate into your next hire.
aboutPage.europe1: TechExpats began as the Israeli tech network in the Netherlands and grew into one of Europe's most connected professional communities. That network is real, and it is international: people building careers and companies across the continent, not in one city or one nationality.
aboutPage.europe2: I work in English, Dutch, and Hebrew, and I spend my days translating between working cultures: Israeli directness, Dutch consensus, the wider European code. For anyone moving into or across Europe, that fluency is often the difference between a stalled search and a great one.
aboutPage.how1: I take on a small number of people and companies at a time. Every engagement starts with an honest conversation about what success really looks like, and I will tell you early if I am not the right person to help. The work is personal, direct, and built to last past the first decision.
aboutPage.close1: If you are planning your next move, or your next hire, I would like to hear about it. The first conversation is free and there is no pitch.
aboutPage.fact1: Based in Amsterdam, working across the Netherlands and Europe
aboutPage.fact2: Career coaching for individuals and headhunting for companies

howItWorks.title: Your path to the right role.
howItWorks.lead: Not another job. The role. A boutique, hands-on, end-to-end process built to actually make it happen. Here is how it works.
howItWorks.delLead: Full, end-to-end guidance. These are the concrete deliverables and tools you receive along the way, not generic advice.
howItWorks.del1d: The document that distils who you are, what you've done, and where you want to go. Everything else is built from it.
howItWorks.del2d: A sharp CV, rewritten around your positioning and the market you're aiming at.
howItWorks.del3d: A LinkedIn profile that draws the right people and tells the right story about you.
howItWorks.del4d: A focused target-company list, with the right person to reach and the hook for each one.
howItWorks.del5d: A personal portal that holds your whole search, and the 'Seven-a-Day' app that turns the method into a daily practice.
howItWorks.del6d: How to reach the right hiring manager (not HR, not easy-apply), and what to write so they reply.
howItWorks.del7d: Real preparation and simulations: how to tell your story, handle hard questions, and read the room.
howItWorks.del8d: Close support on take-home tasks and assignments, so you arrive ready and stand out.
howItWorks.del9d: The line stays open throughout. Send a message, and the system and the guidance move with you.
howItWorks.ideaLead: Job searching is a profession in itself, and most of us never learned it. Until now you have sent your CV to many places, reached late stages, and somehow it did not close. That is not because of you, and it is not the CV. It is because the front door, the open role, is the most crowded door in the building.
howItWorks.p1d: Doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result is the definition of being stuck. The first move is to stop scattering CVs and switch to surgical work.
howItWorks.p2t: The CV is only the output
howItWorks.p2d: You can polish the output only so far. The real leverage is the input: a deep profile that distils all of your skills, drives, and ambitions. Everything else is built from it.
howItWorks.p3t: Find the role, not a job
howItWorks.p3d: The goal is not somewhere that will 'do'. It is the place where your experience, your ambitions, the location, and the flexibility that matters to you all line up.
howItWorks.ideaBottom: In a market flooded with candidates, it is hard to stand out through the pile. Instead of hitting the same nail with the same hammer, we build a method: who the right employers are, how to reach the right person inside them, and how to make them say 'where did this person come from?'
howItWorks.stagesLead: The process runs in three simple stages, in a fixed order. We do not skip, and we do not reverse it: each stage rests on the one before.
howItWorks.s1d: Together we build the one document that becomes the engine of the whole search: a deep, honest picture of who you are, what you have done, and where you genuinely want to go. It stays private, but everything else is built from it.
howItWorks.s1goal: The output: a deep profile that drives everything else.
howItWorks.s2d: From that profile we build a short, deliberately narrow list of the employers who genuinely fit you. The focus is on the right places, not on whoever happens to be advertising. The thinking behind that list is half the value.
howItWorks.s2goal: The output: a focused list of the right employers to go after.
howItWorks.s3t: The engagement, the plan in motion
howItWorks.s3d: This is where most of the time goes, and where the real craft lives. We reach the right people in the right way, so the conversation starts on your terms. How we do that is what we build together.
howItWorks.s3goal: The output: real relationships and the momentum that leads to a role.
howItWorks.orderText: The instinct is to chase open roles. We work the other way around, and that one reversal changes almost everything. Where the open role sits in this order tells you most of what you need to know.
howItWorks.rhythmLead: The program runs about three months, the average time to find a role. Lately I see people landing faster, but nothing can be promised. Within that window there is no stopper: we meet as much as needed, and the line stays open.
howItWorks.ph1d: We build the profile and the target list at high intensity, to finish fast and free up most of the time for the real work.
howItWorks.ph2d: Most of the time lives here: running the plan, outreach, introductions, interviews. Intensive, not anecdotal.
howItWorks.ph3d: Interview preparation, help with take-home assignments, negotiation support, and introductions from my network when they genuinely fit.
howItWorks.rhythmNoteLabel: Why every step counts, even when it does not close immediately
howItWorks.rhythmNote: It is not zero or one. Every step moves you toward a role, even outreach that did not 'produce' one straight away. The relationships you create and the name that becomes known add up to a critical mass. Sometimes it does not close within three months, and then in the fourth month it suddenly happens.
howItWorks.inclLead: Holistic and end-to-end. It accompanies the whole process, not just part of it.
howItWorks.incl1: A personal profile and your positioning
howItWorks.incl2: A focused employer list, with the right person and hook for each
howItWorks.incl3: An outreach plan and its day-to-day execution
howItWorks.incl5: Help with take-home assignments and tasks
howItWorks.incl7: Introductions from my network in the Netherlands, when there is a genuine fit
howItWorks.contractHeading: What it takes, from both of us
howItWorks.contractLead: Let me say this honestly up front: this is not delegation. You are not paying someone to hand you an employment contract when it is ready. It is shared, demanding, intensive work that asks a lot of both of us.
howItWorks.bring1: High availability, the line stays open, no stopper on the number of meetings
howItWorks.bring2: A structured methodology and a system behind every step
howItWorks.bring3: A real network and introductions in the Netherlands, when relevant
howItWorks.bring4: Surgical, end-to-end guidance, not generic tips
howItWorks.ask1: At least an hour a day of effort, beyond meetings and interviews
howItWorks.ask2: Do the homework, even when it is tough and draining
howItWorks.ask3: Openness and attention, especially in the deep profile work
howItWorks.ask4: Energy that rises over time, not falls. That is the real challenge
howItWorks.honest: I do not promise a job. Promising a job would be irresponsible; there is no such thing. My numbers are very good, but there is also luck, demand, and industry, a million things that are not only up to us. What I can say: good people find roles.
howItWorks.ctaHeading: Ready to find the role, not a job?
howItWorks.ctaBody: If your search is not moving the way it should, let's talk. The first conversation is free and there is no pitch.
howItWorks.closing: Find the role, not a job. Reach a person, not a posting.

forCompanies.sub: Some roles are too senior, too specialised, or too important for a job board. I find the people who are not looking, assess them properly, and present a short list you can actually decide from.
forCompanies.problemHeading: Why the usual search falls short
forCompanies.problemBody: The best people are rarely applying. Job boards surface who is available, not who is right. And a mis-hire in a key seat is the most expensive mistake a team can make. High-stakes search is a different craft from filling a vacancy.
forCompanies.processHeading: A search built for the roles that matter.
forCompanies.s1d: We start with the real problem behind the hire, not just the job description: what has been tried, why it failed, and what success looks like in twelve months.
forCompanies.s2t: Reach the people who are not looking
forCompanies.s2d: I go into a network built since 2018 and approach strong passive candidates directly, discreetly, and on your behalf. This is where the work is.
forCompanies.s3d: You get a small, vetted shortlist, each candidate spoken with and assessed for fit, not a stack of CVs. You spend your time deciding, not filtering.
forCompanies.w4: Roles where conventional recruiters have already failed
forCompanies.whyHeading: A recruiter who has sat on your side, and the candidate's.
forCompanies.whyBody: I coach senior professionals every week, so I understand what actually moves a strong candidate, and I can have the honest conversation that turns a passive prospect into your next hire. That is rare, and it is the difference between a CV and a fit.
forCompanies.ctaBody: Tell me about the search. I will assess whether it is a fit for my network and current capacity, and respond within 24 hours.
forCompanies.closing: The right person exists. I know how to reach them.
